items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation
to repair or replacement of damaged residential lateral sewer and water pipes
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4118

SPONSOR: LIU
 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Homeowners shall be reimbursed the full cost of any repairs that are the
result damages from a third party.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. The administrative code of the city of New York is amended by
adding two new sections 24-316.1 and 24-531 to read as follows:

§  24-316.1  Water  lateral  pipe repair or replacement. The City of New
York shall be responsible for the repair or replacement of  all  damages
residential  lateral water pipes where such pipes have been damaged as a
result of actions or negligence of the City of New  York  or  a  utility
company.

§ 24- 531 Sewer lateral pipe repair or replacement. The City of New York
shall  be responsible for the repair or replacement of all damaged resi-
dential lateral water pipes where such pipes  have  been  damaged  as  a
result  of  actions  or  negligence of the City of New York or a utility
company.

Section 2. This act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Title 15 of the Rules of the City of New York places the financial  cost
of  inoperative or defective lines on the responsibility of the homeown-
er, in which they are forced to comply within 30 days  of  being  issued
the  order,  which  unsatisfied  will  result  in  shutting off of water
service. The cost to the homeowner, which can amount to ten of thousands
of dollars is a financial hardship that should not  be  endured  when  a
third  party  is at fault.  Homeowners should not be burdened by damages
and costs that are no fault of their own but at the  fault  of  a  third
party,  including  but  not  limited  to city infrastructure and private
utility companies.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

new bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4118B

SPONSOR: LIU
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the administrative code of the city of
New York, in relation to repair or replacement of damaged residential
lateral sewer and water pipes

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To hold public utilities responsible for sewage and water pipe repairs
when it has been determined that the utility is responsible for damages

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. The administrative code of the city of New York is amended by
adding two new sections 24-316.1 and 24531 to read as follows:

24-316.1 Water lateral pipe repair or replacement Any public utility
company as defined in section two of the public service law shall be
responsible for the repair or replacement of all damaged residential
lateral water pipes where such pipes have been damaged as a result of
the actions or negligence of such public utility company as determined
by the department of environmental protection of the city of New York..

24-531 Sewer lateral pipe repair or replacement Any public utility
company as defined in section two of the public service law shall be
responsible for the repair or replacement of all damaged residential
lateral sewer pipes where such pipes have been damaged as a result of
the actions or negligence of such public utility company as determined
by the department of environmental protection of the city of New York.

Section 2. This act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Title 15 of the Rules of the City of New York places the financial cost
of inoperative or defective water lines on the responsibility of the
homeowner, in which they are forced to comply within 30 days of being
issued the order. If the order is unsatisfied, it will result in the
shutting off of water service. The cost to the homeowner, which can
amount to ten of thousands of dollars is a financial hardship that
should not be endured when a third party, such as a public utility, is
at fault. Homeowners should not be burdened by damages and costs that
are of no fault of their own but the fault of a third party, including
but not limited to public utility companies.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

C.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation
to repair or replacement of damaged residential lateral sewer and water pipes
C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4118C

SPONSOR: LIU
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the administrative code of the city of
New York, in relation to repair or replacement of damaged residential
lateral sewer and water pipes

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To hold public utilities responsible for sewage and water pipe repairs
when it has been determined that the utility is responsible for damages

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Title 15 of the Rules of the City of New York places the financial cost
of inoperative or defective water lines on the responsibility of the
homeowner, in which they are forced to comply within 30 days of being
issued the order. If the order is unsatisfied, it will result in the
shutting off of water service.

In at least 2 locations in New York City, 188th Street, Queens, and 3521
Avenue D, Brooklyn have experienced multiple water and sewer pipe leaks
due to corrosion by underground stray electrical current, both deemed to
have been caused by infrastructure managed by a public utility. Another
possible site along Winchester Blvd. in Queens is showing a similar
pattern of multiple water leaks.

These leaks are incredibly damaging to our cities roads and infrastruc-
ture. As well, under current law, the homeowners still bear the respon-
sibility and financial cost of repeatedly replacing their water pipes,
despite determinations by the Departmental of Environmental Protection
that a public utility is at fault. Without any ability to cure the stray
current causing damage to their water pipes, the homeowners at each site
have been force to continually replace their pipes or experiment with
different technology in hopes of preventing the continual leaks. Some
homeowners have had to replace their pipes up to 3 times. The cost to
some of the homeowners, has been over ten thousand dollars each.

Homeowners should not be burdened by damages and costs that are of no
fault of their own but are the fault of a public utility company, whose
are responsible for maintaining their own infrastructure.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 217
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 4118-C, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in
      relation  to  repair or replacement of damaged residential lateral
      sewer and water pipes"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would vest the New York  City  Department  of  Environmental
Protection  (DEP)  with the authority to investigate whether the infras-
tructure, electric current, or other activity of a public utility compa-
ny was the cause of significant damage to residential  water  and  sewer
pipes.  The bill would also permit DEP to impose the costs of repair and
replacement of damaged pipes on public utility companies. The DEP  would
be  the  sole  arbiter of damages and the bill would require the cooper-
ation of public utility companies with any requests made  by  DEP.    In
addition,  the  utility  companies  would  be responsible for paying for
DEP's costs.
 
  The bill, which adopts a muddled liability  standard  for  a  specific
type  of  property  damage  claims,  does  not contain basic due process
provisions such as the right to a hearing, the right of  affected  home-
owners  to  intervene,  and  the  right  to appeal DEP's decision, among
numerous other shortcomings. The bill further  does  not  recognize  the
potential  for a conflict of interest since the authority to investigate
public utilities and collect costs  would  be  triggered  by  DEP's  own
actions.
 
  When  a  public  utility  causes  damage to water or sewer pipes, that
utility should have to bear the cost of repairing  the  harm  they  have
caused.  However,  replacing  the current method of determining fault in
this way is inadvisable, unfair, and inefficient.
 
  Due to the fact that the bill provides  an  incomplete  legal  remedy,
fails  to  provide  basic  due  process protections, and would raise the
potential for a conflict of interest, this bill must be vetoed.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
